messages:
maria (AE): Hey team — large enterprise wants MFN-like language and a retro price protection if we lower list rates within 18 months. they want this to cover Dedicated/Dedicated+ tiers. asking if we can agree without blowing up the commit economics.

ajay (Presales): quick context: they want a 60-day POC then go GA. no initial commit, but will commit post-POC if numbers look good. their procurement says MFN to ensure parity with future public promos.

diana (Deal Desk): tagging @andrew (Legal) and @kyle (Finance). we'll need deal desk approval for any concession that impacts tiered pricing or caps. if we add retro protection we need clear cap (e.g., max refund or credit). :eyes:

andrew (Legal): High level: MFN clauses are doable but scary if broad. we prefer a scoped MFN: 1) limit to equivalent product configuration 2) timebox (12 months post-signature) 3) exclude one-off promotions and partner/channel discounts. also recommend an explicit cap on credits (either $ or % of committed spend).

kyle (Finance): numbers: rough calc — their ARR lands us at Tier 3 pricing. if we allow full retro protection with no cap, downside could be ~20-30% of first-year committed revenue in credits if we drop public rates. propose a cap = min(3 months of committed spend, $250k).

maria (AE): they pushed back on caps in last call. procurement says caps defeat the purpose. they want assurance they won't be undercut by later promos.

ajay (Presales): technical blocker: if MFN covers Dedicated+ (custom infra), we could be forced to match favorable pricing that applies only to very different capacity profiles. ops can’t replicate that margin. also POC-specific discounts shouldn't propagate — suggest explicit carve-out for POC/intro credits.

andrew (Legal): Proposed redline snippet below — keeps MFN narrow and adds a capped remedy. happy to paste into redline.

```
MFN: For a period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Redwood will offer the Customer pricing no less favorable than Redwood offers to any other customer for substantially similar product configurations ("Comparable Offerings"). Comparable Offerings shall exclude: (a) time-limited promotional offers, (b) one-off POC or trial credits, and (c) channel/partner-discounted rates. Remedy for breach shall be limited to a credit to the Customer not to exceed the lesser of (i) three (3) months of the Customer's committed spend, or (ii) $250,000.
```

diana (Deal Desk): this is reasonable for approval flow. if sales accepts this language we can fast-track to pricing committee. would like explicit confirmation from Finance on the cap numbers.

kyle (Finance): confirmed — the cap numbers are conservative and protect unit economics for Dedicated variants. :white_check_mark:

maria (AE): i'll take this back to procurement. one ask: can we temporarily apply a promo-exclusion clause to GA pricing for the first 6 months to avoid immediate comparisons?

andrew (Legal): we can add a 6-month promotional carve-out in the same clause — short phrase, ok to include. I'll prepare the redline and drop in the doc now.

presales-bot: Document uploaded: /contracts/ACME-Redwood-2026/redline_v3.pdf :file_folder:

maria (AE): thanks everyone — keeping thread here. will update after procurement sync. :pray:
